(16:41 hrs)

Honourable Members, I now provide the floor to the Honourable Minister of Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, to present the proposal for discussion on the Asset Laundering (Prevention) (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, received with a message from the House of Representatives along with the committee's report.

Thank you.

Honourable Members in favour of this proposal, say "Aye".
- "Aye"
Honourable Members against this proposal, say "Nay".
No voice of "Nay" was heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal to discuss the Asset Laundering (Prevention) (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, received with a message from the House of Representatives along with the report of the Legislation Management Committee, has been unanimously approved.
Honourable Members, discussion will now take place on the Asset Laundering (Prevention) (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, received with a message from the House of Representatives along with the report of the Legislation Management Committee. I inform you that discussion can only be held on the committee's report, the clauses of the bill related thereto, and other related clauses.
I request Honourable Members who wish to speak to submit their names within two minutes. I have allocated three minutes to each Honourable Member participating in the discussion. Honourable Member Khamma Bahadur Khati.
Honourable Mr. Khamma Bahadur Khati (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson, Honourable Ministers, and Honourable Members, I wish to raise a few points regarding the Asset Laundering (Prevention) (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083. Firstly, regarding the Asset Laundering (Prevention) (Third Amendment) Bill, there was extensive discussion in the Legislation Committee. The Honourable Minister of Finance was also directly involved, and with his consultation and suggestions, the proposals we put forth were limited to two clauses. The Minister also facilitated the process in a very easy and straightforward manner. Feedback was received from all Honourable Members. This alone is not enough; there are many shortcomings. These will be addressed later in a manner that adapts to the time, circumstances, and events. However, considering the discussion we had and the amendments we proposed for swift justice, incorporating the points raised by all Honourable Members of the Legislation Committee, it was agreed that Clause 13, Sub-clause 1, Clause (c) should remain as per the previous provision, and similarly, regarding Clause 22, Sub-clause 1, the publication by the Attorney General's Office, rather than the Nepal Government publishing a notice in the Gazette, was agreed upon, as the latter seemed to be an encroachment of jurisdiction.
Thus, through discussions among the Ministers and Honourable Members, we have reached a conclusion. This has taken concrete form. In the coming days, our challenge was that due to insufficient time, many Honourable Members could not express their views. The time was short. It is commendable that we have worked to expedite the process of amending existing laws and regulations received from the House of Representatives, ensuring that this bill comes in time in the future and the discussion process continues in this manner, with the Upper House facilitating not only by keeping the public at the center of policy and regulatory matters but also by strengthening efforts to amend the existing laws and regulations.
I have expressed these points. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members, the discussion on the proposal to discuss the Asset Laundering (Prevention) (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, received with a message from the House of Representatives along with the report of the Legislation Management Committee, concludes here.

I will not say much. Honourable Khamma Bahadur Khati has already spoken. We have advanced this law-making process in a cordial and judicious manner. I hope we can continue this in the future as well. The National Assembly holds a special place in our federal parliament. It is known as the 'Upper House', and we expect constructive support from the Honourable Members here. I believe that even amidst time constraints and the pressure of balancing national needs, we have found an excellent way forward, which will help the country progress. Therefore, I extend my heartfelt thanks to the Honourable Members, the Right Honourable Chairperson, and all the staff. Thank you.

Honorable Mr. Renu Chand (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson,
(16:56 hrs) Sir, forcing the passage of bills in such haste impacts the quality of laws. The bill was being amended as it went through the committee. We are forced to pass this in haste and bear the responsibility for its legal consequences, Mr. Speaker. We have new colleagues in this government, they at least have the convenience of being new, but we don't even have that. When the public questions us later, asking what we were doing, the moral responsibility will fall entirely on us. Therefore, I urge the respected Chairperson, the honorable Chairperson, and the government not to put us in such a situation in the future.
For example, what happens when we are not allowed to read, when we are not given adequate time? For instance, it was written in Clause 33 (b) that there will be a Government Procurement Service Office under the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers. Provisions like these show a lack of understanding of federalism and interfere with the jurisdiction of provincial and local governments, so extensive discussions were held and some improvements were made. The National Assembly is the house of federalism. When such issues arise, we must be accountable to our people and to our electorate.
Although the facilitation by the ministers was beneficial to us. However, if it had been passed without allowing us to read, when we go to the electorate, they will ask us, "You were old, experienced. What did you do?" and we would not have a moral standing. Such matters need to be considered in the future, this is my request.
The government also needs to understand that the Legislation Committee, the National Assembly, is an opportunity to correct its mistakes and flaws in the law. The National Assembly has its nature and history. It has always facilitated and refined the work of the government. Therefore, even though this act has come in a hurry and we have not been able to discuss it extensively, with the cooperation of all of us, the government ministers, the committee chairperson, the committee members, and the amendment proposers, through extensive discussion - extensive because we are compelled to use the word now, having sat from morning till evening. However, even that morning-to-evening sitting was not enough. Keeping this in mind for the future, I would like to thank the ministers, the committee chairperson, the members, and all the amendment proposers. I urge you to pass this, thank you.

Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal (Nepal Communist Party, UML): (17:08 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, we are now going to have further discussions on the Bill to Amend the Cooperatives Act, 2074, which is the Cooperatives Bill, 2083, after it has come from the Legislation Management Committee. I myself and 9 other honorable members had submitted amendments to various clauses in this Legislation Management Committee. Honorable members who proposed amendments, honorable members of the committee, the leadership of the ministry, and the honorable minister himself, along with the concerned civil servants, we had intense discussions and interactions, and our common objective, the objective of the honorable members, the objective of the honorable members who proposed amendments, and the objective of the ministry's leadership, was to make this bill better, how to make it more advanced and refined. Therefore, our participation there was meaningful, all of our participation was meaningful, and the ministry truly took ownership. It took ownership, and most of the issues raised by us, most of the issues raised by the honorable members who proposed amendments, have been addressed. Our concern was singular. We remained focused on this direction. Therefore, despite the time constraints, we had intense discussions and interactions day and night, and it has been presented to the house after being passed unanimously. Therefore, I request and urge all honorable members to pass this bill unanimously, and I also thank the honorable minister and all the staff of the entire Parliament Secretariat. Thank you. Honorable Mr. Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, (17:21 hrs) We discussed the Bill to Amend Some Nepal Acts related to Health Sciences Institute, 2083 in the Legislation Management Committee yesterday, and in a short time, we reached some decisions by having a concentrated discussion to make it as good as possible, and since the Honorable Minister of Health and Population has taken ownership of the amendment proposals raised by us, the amendment proposers, on behalf of the government, we also support it. In this short period leading up to the passing stage, the committee members, under the leadership of the Chairperson of the Legislative Management Committee, have actively played their roles. Similarly, I express my heartfelt thanks to the honorable members of the assembly, the relevant honorable ministers, the civil servants of the committee secretariat, and the employees of the concerned bodies for the remarkable roles they have played. It is expected that the committee will continue to be active in enhancing the dignity of the National Assembly in the future. Today, the National Assembly can proudly state that it has succeeded in discussing four replacement bills in the committee and sending them to the House of Representatives after passing them in the assembly today, along with the committee's reports, and two dependent bills (the Finance Bill, 2083 and the Debt Raising Bill, 2083) have been discussed and passed in the assembly and sent to the House of Representatives. Finally, I would like to thank everyone again.

Honorable members, according to Article 94 of the Constitution of Nepal, constitutional bodies shall submit their annual reports to the President, and the President shall cause that report to be presented to the Federal Parliament through the Prime Minister. Similarly, the constitution also provides that the heads and officials of constitutional bodies shall be accountable and responsible to the Federal Parliament. In accordance with that provision, reports from constitutional bodies have been continuously presented to the National Assembly by the government. As per the provision in Rule 217 (c) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, the Business Advisory Committee has decided on Ashad 15, 2083, to commence the practice of discussing reports in the assembly. Therefore, the discussion and recommendations on the annual report of the National Inclusion Commission for the fiscal year 2081/082, which has been presented to the assembly, will be held in the meeting on Ashad 26, 2083, tomorrow. Therefore, I also expect the active participation of the honorable members in tomorrow's discussion.
